title.value: Learning Lyapunov-Stable Polynomial Dynamical Systems Through Imitation
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Learning Lyapunov-Stable Polynomial Dynamical Systems Through Imitation

extractions.description: The paper introduces a method for learning a globally stable nonlinear dynamical system as a motion planning policy using polynomial dynamical systems (PLYDS) and Lyapunov stability theory, demonstrating its effectiveness in robotic manipulation tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper focuses on robotics and control systems, it does not explicitly address sustainable development themes or goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Imitation learning is a paradigm to address complex motion planning problems by learning a policy to imitate an expert’s behavior. However, relying solely on the expert’s data might lead to unsafe actions when the robot deviates from the demonstrated trajectories. Stability guarantees have previously been provided utilizing nonlinear dynamical systems, acting as high-level motion planners, in conjunction with the Lyapunov stability theorem. Yet, these methods are prone to inaccurate policies, high computational cost, sample inefficiency, or quasi stability when replicating complex and highly nonlinear trajectories. To mitigate this problem, we present an approach for learning a globally stable nonlinear dynamical system as a motion planning policy. We model the nonlinear dynamical system as a parametric polynomial and learn the polynomial’s coefficients jointly with a Lyapunov candidate. To showcase its success, we compare our method against the state of the art in simulation and conduct real-world experiments with the Kinova Gen3 Lite manipulator arm. Our experiments demonstrate the sample efficiency and reproduction accuracy of our method for various expert trajectories, while remaining stable in the face of perturbations.

primary_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on robotics, control systems, and imitation learning, rather than on any specific Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development category.
